Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Quickdraw parties

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

A configured RQ_ROOM_SERVICE enables Create party, Join party and Rejoin recent. The shared Replay Party component durably stores enrollment and invitations before opening the game. It configures Room, authenticated signaling and the appropriate native ENet or browser WebRTC backend. Personal identity/name preferences remain separate from each party's gameplay credential.

Invited members are trusted peers by this example's explicit policy: they may receive complete checkpoints and host a successor session. Watch-only play retains seat zero and disables checkpoint reception. The watch preference does not revoke membership permissions granted by the invite. This is a player-hosted model, not a claim of cheat-resistant hosting or public account authentication.

The scene uses the same typed Quickdraw world, controls/actions and presentation on native and browser builds. The first connected player starts the waiting duel. Planned handoff is available to the active authority once a successor is prepared. Unexpected authority loss uses Room's existing lease, rollback and recovery policy. A returning host can use its retained profile and Rejoin recent in a fresh process.

Browser identities, display names and party credentials use their existing shared IndexedDB components. Native parties use the optional SQLite adapter; RQ_ROOMS_DB selects its database. RQ_PROFILE still selects the separate native personal profile. Native direct-address and file-save paths remain available when no service is configured. Browser direct ENet launch is refused with an explanation; use a configured party. Browser solo play shares the model and now has separate local save slots in the standalone menu. Party publication does not write those slots.

Defaults require verified WSS. RQ_ROOM_LOCAL=1 permits explicit loopback WS development. RQ_ROOM_ADDRESS and RQ_PORT define the advertised native endpoint. ICE settings come from RQ_ICE_JSON, or RQ_ROOM_RELAY=1 requests authenticated relay credentials. Do not combine both ICE sources. Public deployment and non-loopback routing need their own acceptance; localhost success does not establish reachability across the internet.

The bundled room service recognizes Quickdraw content D2 when selected by the operator and supplies its typed checkpoint backend. A live online authority's Save/F5 publishes through Room rather than writing a local file. RQ_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MS optionally sets the shared publication interval; zero keeps it manual. Native file resume still refuses coordinated archives. No gameplay content/schema change is introduced by this integration.

Published checkpoints also support an abandoned party. A fresh trusted player uses Rejoin recent; if no authority remains, Room loads the saved publication and requests a guarded restore grant before creating a new session. The same published tick is retained under a new epoch, and other saved members can reclaim their seats. An observer must explicitly select Watch only and waits for a restored host rather than restoring authority. The UI distinguishes saved-party restoration from a live handoff. This path is covered by tests/replay_quickdraw_party_restore/run.sh, including a service restart on the existing database. Public deployment and broader restore races remain separate acceptance work.

The native whole-party path is also covered by tests/replay_quickdraw_native_restore/run.sh, using individual SQLite credential stores, a trusted local WSS certificate and separate ENet gameplay endpoints. Both the native and browser fixtures kill all game processes and restart the service on its existing database before restoring and republishing.

The recovery notice uses the shared backup-status observation. It distinguishes an approved backup from preparation, stale progress or uncertain control; a prior host change does not imply the next backup is ready.
